p: Science Oxford's discovery centre sits at Stansfeld Park in Headington, and while you're out this way, there's a surprising amount to see. The most famous sight is the Headington Shark, a huge fibreglass shark that appears to have crashed head-first through the roof of a terraced house on New High Street. Installed in 1986, it's become one of Oxford's best-loved landmarks and makes a great photo stop.

Bury Knowle Park, in the heart of Headington, has a playground, gardens and plenty of space for a picnic, while Shotover Country Park, on the edge of the city, offers woodland walks and big views over the surrounding countryside. Both are ideal for burning off any leftover energy after a morning of experiments.
Headington itself has a lively high street with cafés, bakeries and independent shops, so you won't be short of places for lunch.

A tip for parents: science centres like this work best when children are encouraged to ask their own questions. Rather than steering them to the 'right' answer, ask them what they think will happen before they try an experiment. It turns a fun morning into real learning, and you might just learn something yourself. Easy, brainy and a little bit bonkers, Headington makes a smashing half-day.
